svg.text: Solid = built and tested, dashed = planned. On the modules, go by the silkscreen labels.
Pin order on your module may differ:
Wire by the labels printed on each
sensor PCB, not by the cable plug order.
3.3 V only, never 5 V. Measured: S reads
HIGH when the beam is blocked.
1. Switch the 12 V on first, then power or reset the ESP32.
The sketches configure the driver only at boot.
2. Never connect or disconnect the motor with the 12 V on.
3. Common ground: brick −, driver GND and ESP32 GND are joined.
4. PDN_UART: GPIO16 and the resistor from GPIO17 meet at the 4th pin.
The 5th pin has the same label but is not connected to the chip.
5. Coils: red + green = coil 1 (OA1, OA2), blue + black = coil 2 (OB1, OB2).
Both wires of a motor coil go to the same driver coil.
6. Fuse and e-stop are planned. The e-stop cuts the motor supply only.
7. Fit hard stops beyond each sensor: a sensor that loses power reads clear.
8. 400 mA is a bench setting. Raise it for the loaded boom (driver max 1.2 A RMS).
9. Buttons (GPIO TBD) and a second axis are not drawn yet.
